Rashi on Sotah 25a:10:1.hebrew: תלא רחמנא - דכתיב: וקנא את אשתו:
Rashi on Sotah 25a:10:1.english: The Merciful One made it dependent - For it is written: "and he shall be jealous of his wife."

Rashi on Sotah 25a:10:2.hebrew: או דלמא כיון דקפיד קפיד - כלומר, כיון דאורחיה דבעל למיקפד בהכי, על כרחיה דהאי נמי הויא קפידא לגביה:
Rashi on Sotah 25a:10:2.english: Or perhaps, since he is particular, he is particular - That is to say, since it is the way of a husband to be particular about this, necessarily this [husband] too has a [genuine] objection regarding it.

Rashi on Sotah 25a:11:1.hebrew: עבדינן מילתא דדלמא לא ניחא ליה - והיאך אנו נעשים שלוחים לו בדבר שהוא חוב לו, שאינו חפץ בו? וקיימא לן (כתובות דף יא.) דאין חבין לאדם שלא בפניו:
Rashi on Sotah 25a:11:1.english: Are we doing something that perhaps he does not want? - How can we become his agents in a matter that is to his detriment, which he does not desire? And we hold (Ketubot 11a) that one may not act to another's detriment in his absence.

Rashi on Sotah 25a:12:1.hebrew: שמחל על קנויו - והשתא ס"ד דקבעי בין שמחל קודם סתירה בין שמחל לאחר הסתירה. ואם תימצי לומר עוברת על דת שרצה לקיימה מקיימה, הני מילי בלא קינוי; אבל היכא דאיכא קינוי וסתירה ורצה למחול, מהו? מי עקר קינוי ושריא ליה, או לאו:
Rashi on Sotah 25a:12:1.english: Who forgave his warning - And now it enters one's mind that he is asking [about both cases], whether he forgave before the seclusion or forgave after the seclusion. And if you should say that a woman who transgresses the law, [and] her husband wished to maintain [the marriage with] her, may be maintained [by him] — this applies only where there was no warning. But where there was a warning and a seclusion, and he wished to forgive, what is the law? Does he uproot the warning, so that she is permitted to him, or not?

Rashi on Sotah 25a:13:1.hebrew: עבדינן מידי דאתי בעל ומחיל - ואיכא זילותא דבי דינא:
Rashi on Sotah 25a:13:1.english: Do we do something [such that] the husband might come and forgive - and there is a disgrace to the court.

Rashi on Sotah 25a:13:2.hebrew: סתמא דמילתא אדם מסכים כו' - וסמכינן אסתם דעתיה דאינשי, ומקנינן לה. ואי אתי ומחיל, מחיל:
Rashi on Sotah 25a:13:2.english: The ordinary nature of the matter is that a person agrees, etc. - And we rely on the ordinary presumption about people's thinking, and we transfer ownership to her. And if he comes and waives [his claim], he has waived it.

Rashi on Sotah 25a:15:1.hebrew: מאי שנא תלמידי חכמים - תירוצא הוא, והכי קאמר: לעולם מחיל, ודיקא ליה ממתני'. מאי שנא דבעינן תלמידי חכמים? משום דגמירי דאסורה ליה בדלא מחיל קינוי, ואי אתי למיבעל אמרין ליה: אחלי לקינויך:
Rashi on Sotah 25a:15:1.english: What is different about Torah scholars? - This is an answer, and this is what it means: Actually, he can waive [his warning], and [the questioner] derives this from the mishnah. [The answer is:] Why is it that we require Torah scholars? Because they know that she is forbidden to him if he did not waive the warning, and if he comes to have relations with her, they will say to him: Waive your warning.

Rashi on Sotah 25a:16:1.hebrew: סח לי זעירא - שהיה מאנשי ירושלים:
Rashi on Sotah 25a:16:1.english: Ze'ira told me - For he was one of the people of Jerusalem.

Rashi on Sotah 25a:16:2.hebrew: זקן ממרא - שהמרה על ב"ד של לשכת הגזית, ומיתתו בחנק:
Rashi on Sotah 25a:16:2.english: A rebellious elder - Who rebelled against the court of the Chamber of Hewn Stone, and his death is by strangulation.

Rashi on Sotah 25a:19:1.hebrew: שהיא בלאו - אחרי אשר הוטמאה. לרבות סוטה שנסתרה, בפ"ק דיבמות (דף יא:):
Rashi on Sotah 25a:19:1.english: That she is [subject to] a prohibition - After she has been defiled. [This comes] to include a sotah who secluded herself, in the first chapter of Yevamot (11b).

Rashi on Sotah 25a:1:1.hebrew: ושמואל דאמר אנא דאמרי אפי' לרבי יאשיה - דאמר שותה. דמדאצטריך לרבויי לשתיה, ש"מ לאו אשתו היא — ליורשה, וליטמא לה, ולהאכילה תרומה. וכ"ש לרבי יונתן דאמר אינה שותה, משום דלאו אשתו היא. והא דאיצטריך למעוטי, אסמכתא בעלמא היא, ולאו דקרא להכי אתא, אלא להקיש אשה לאיש כדשני לעיל:
Rashi on Sotah 25a:1:1.english: And Shmuel who said: I who said [this holds] even according to Rabbi Yoshiya - who said that she drinks. For since it was necessary to include her in the drinking, [we learn] that she is not his wife — to inherit her, to become impure for her, and to feed her terumah. And certainly [this holds] according to Rabbi Yonatan, who said that she does not drink, because she is not his wife. And the fact that it was necessary to exclude her is merely a textual support (asmakhta); the verse did not come for this purpose, but rather to draw an analogy between a woman and a man, as [the Gemara] answered above.

Rashi on Sotah 25a:22:1.english: In what do they disagree? - What reason do they give for their words?

Rashi on Sotah 25a:22:2.hebrew: ב"ש סברי שטר העומד לגבות כגבוי דמי - מי שיש לו שטר חוב על חבירו ושיעבד לו בו נכסיו, מוחזק בעל השטר בנכסים יותר מן הלוה. והלכך, כיון דנכסי ברשותיה קיימי, הוו להו יורשי הבעל תובעין, והמוציא מחבירו עליו הראיה, ועליהן להביא ראיה שזינתה בסתירה זו ואבדה כתובתה:
Rashi on Sotah 25a:22:2.english: Beit Shammai hold that a document that is destined to be collected is considered as though it has already been collected - One who has a promissory note against another, in which [the borrower] pledged his property to him, the holder of the note is considered to have a stronger hold on the property than the borrower. Therefore, since the property is in her possession, the husband's heirs are the claimants, and the burden of proof is upon the one who seeks to extract [money] from another. Thus it is upon them to bring proof that she committed adultery through this seclusion and forfeited her marriage contract.

Rashi on Sotah 25a:2:1.hebrew: עוברת על דת - יהודית שאינה צנועה, יוצאה וראשה פרועה, וטווה בשוק, ומדברת עם כל אדם, דאמר בכתובות בפרק המדיר (כתובות דף עב.) דיוצאה שלא בכתובה:
Rashi on Sotah 25a:2:1.english: One who transgresses the law - A Jewish woman who is not modest: she goes out with her head uncovered, spins in the marketplace, and speaks with any man, as it says in Ketubot, in the chapter "HaMadir" (Ketubot 72a), that she goes out without her ketubah [i.e., she is divorced without receiving her marriage settlement].

Rashi on Sotah 25a:2:2.hebrew: צריכה התראה - שמא תחזור, ואם תחזור לא תפסיד כתובתה. או אינה צריכה התראה, דבלאו התראה מפסדא:
Rashi on Sotah 25a:2:2.english: Does she require a warning? - [Perhaps a warning is required], lest she return [to proper conduct], and if she returns, she does not forfeit her marriage contract. Or [perhaps] she does not require a warning, for even without a warning she forfeits [it].

Rashi on Sotah 25a:3:1.hebrew: למאי - כיון דלא שתיא, קינוי למאי אהני:
Rashi on Sotah 25a:3:1.english: For what [purpose]? - Since she does not drink, for what [purpose] does the warning help?

Rashi on Sotah 25a:3:2.hebrew: לאפסודי כתובתה - ואי לאו דקני, לא מפסדא. אלמא צריכה התראה, וזו עוברת על דת היא, שנסתרה עם אנשים:
Rashi on Sotah 25a:3:2.english: To cause her to forfeit her marriage contract - And if he had not warned her, she would not forfeit [it]. Evidently, she requires a warning; and this one is a woman who transgresses the law [of modesty], for she secluded herself with men.

Rashi on Sotah 25a:4:1.hebrew: להשקותה כשהיא נשואה - ואם תסתר לאחר נישואין, שותה על ידי קינוי של אירוסין. שאינו יכול להשקותה כשהיא ארוסה, דבעינן "תחת אישה":
Rashi on Sotah 25a:4:1.english: To make her drink when she is married - And if she is secluded [with the man] after the marriage, she drinks on account of the warning issued during the betrothal; for he cannot make her drink while she is [merely] betrothed, since [the verse] requires "under her husband" (Numbers 5:29).

Rashi on Sotah 25a:7:1.hebrew: לאוסרה אבועל - קינוי לא מהני אלא לאוסרה על בועלה, אם ימות זה או יגרשנה ולא שתת:
Rashi on Sotah 25a:7:1.english: To prohibit her to the paramour - The warning is effective only to prohibit her to her paramour, if this one [the husband] dies or divorces her, and she did not drink.

Rashi on Sotah 25a:7:2.hebrew: אלא לפוסלה מכתובתה - מכלל דאי לא אתרו בה, לא מפסדא:
Rashi on Sotah 25a:7:2.english: Rather, to disqualify her from her ketubah - By implication, if they did not warn her, she does not forfeit [it].

Rashi on Sotah 25a:7:3.hebrew: דתנן - לקמן בפרק "כשם שהמים בודקין" (סוטה דף כז:):
Rashi on Sotah 25a:7:3.english: As we learned in a Mishnah - Later, in the chapter "Just as the water tests" (Sotah 27b).

Rashi on Sotah 25a:9:1.english: It is different there - [That is,] this [law] that warning is required.

Rashi on Sotah 25a:9:2.hebrew: דלית לה אימתא דבעל - ואי לאו דאתרו בה בי דינא, לא הוה לן למקנסה. דכיון דלית לה אימתא, אין תימה בדבר אם עוברת על דת, ואין זה פריצותא יתירתא. אבל מי שבעלה אצלה ואינה יראה ממנו ועוברת על דת, פריצותא יתירתא אית בה, ואיכא למימר דבלאו התראה נמי מפסדא כתובתה:
Rashi on Sotah 25a:9:2.english: For she has no fear of a husband - And if not for the fact that the court warned her, we would not have needed to penalize her. For since she has no fear [of a husband], it is no wonder if she transgresses the law, and this is not extra [or excessive] brazenness. But one whose husband is with her, and she does not fear him, and she transgresses the law — there is extra brazenness in her, and one could say that even without a warning she forfeits her marriage contract.

Tosafot on Sotah 25a:17:1.hebrew: שמע מינה בעל שמחל על קינויו קינויו מחול - ותפשוט נמי עוברת על דת: אם רצה בעלה לקיימה — מקיימה, אפילו התרה בה:
Tosafot on Sotah 25a:17:1.english: Learn from this: a husband who waived his warning, his warning is waived - And one should also resolve [the other question, regarding] a woman who transgresses the law (overet al dat): if her husband wishes to keep her [as his wife], he may keep her, even if he had warned her:

Tosafot on Sotah 25a:9:1.hebrew: שאני התם דלית לה אימתא דבעל - וא"ת: הני דבעי למפשט מארוסה ושומרת יבם, לית להו נמי אימתא דבעלה, דהא בעלייהו לאו גבייהו נינהו? י"ל: אפ"ה אית ליה אימתא, פן ירגישו בעליהן בפריצותן:
Tosafot on Sotah 25a:9:1.english: There it is different, for she has no fear of a husband - And if you ask: Those [cases] from which [the Gemara] wished to derive [a proof] — from an betrothed woman and a woman awaiting her yavam — they also have no fear of their husband, for their husbands are not with them? One can answer: Even so, she does have fear, [lest] their husbands become aware of their licentiousness:
